survey.question: On a huge story (like the Rhule firing), what serves you best?

items.title: Deadline day: the Chiefs are expected to be active, with Josh Downs and Calvin Ridley the names to watch before 4 p.m. ET
items.subheader: Worthy's hamstring makes a thin receiver room thinner; Veach told CBS Sunday the conversations continue. James Palmer: 'It was likely KC would add a WR before Tuesday.'
items.image_alt: Xavier Worthy warms up before a game

quotes.text: The Chiefs have been calling on WRs for weeks, and now Xavier Worthy goes down grabbing his hamstring. It was likely KC would add a WR before Tuesday.

items.title: Mahomes is day to day with a throwing-elbow injury, Reid says; Worthy's hamstring projected 'multi-week' by ProFootballDoc
items.subheader: Mahomes finished Sunday's game after David Bailey's strip-sack bent his elbow; Reid called Worthy's injury a 'tweak' while David Chao anticipates multiple weeks out. Atlanta visits Sunday.

items.title: Jaguars go all-in as deadline buyers - likely ending the Brian Thomas Jr. pipe dream - and more moves are expected by 4 p.m. ET
items.subheader: Jacksonville loaded up for an AFC run instead of selling; the Bears already got an impact from Jeffery Simmons, and the Vikings are expected to explore the QB market after Carson Wentz's Monday-night meltdown.

items.title: Rhule on firing Holgorsen: 'We're not scoring enough points'; Glenn Thomas debuts as play-caller Saturday at Rutgers, one win from bowl eligibility
items.subheader: Rhule says the offense isn't broken and won't be torn down; DC Rob Aurich signed a two-year extension with the Blackshirts 12th nationally in total defense. Kickoff 11:30 a.m. CT on BTN.
items.image_alt: Matt Rhule at his Monday press conference

quotes.text: We can point to the yards and stand on we're third in the Big Ten in total offense, fourth in rushing, whatever, those things, but we're not scoring enough points. I felt like the time was now.
I don't think the offense is broken. I don't think we have bad players. I don't think we have bad coaches.

items.title: Browser Use 1.0 deletes 80% of its library - the agent now writes Python straight to Chrome over CDP, scoring up to 33 points higher at 2.7-5.2x lower cost
items.subheader: 'No DOM serializer, no action schema, nothing in between.' Defaults now route to Browser Use's cloud and gateway model; the docs warn model-written code runs as you, so containerize untrusted tasks.

quotes.text: Predefined state and action space make it worse.
An action space is what made a run replayable; a program step gives you effects instead of a diff.
quotes.by: John Rood, on the trade-off, replying to Zunic

items.title: n8n Labs releases Nod: an open-source personal agent with its own local computer and browser that asks before it sends, pays or deletes
items.subheader: Research preview for Mac and Windows; connects Gmail, Calendar, Drive and Slack, runs scheduled jobs, remembers months of conversation (93.2% on LongMemEval) - passwords stay encrypted in forms the model can't read.
items.image_alt: Nod, the personal agent from n8n Labs

items.title: Runpod for Agents: your coding agent can now provision, diagnose and shut down GPU infra itself, via a hosted MCP server and 35 tested skills
items.subheader: Agents already issue over half of all CLI commands on Runpod; plugins ship for Claude Code, Codex and ChatGPT, with destructive actions gated behind developer confirmation. SF-based.

quotes.text: An agent with API access isn't the same as an agent that knows how to run a workload correctly.
quotes.by: Zhen Lu, Runpod CEO and co-founder

items.title: agent-browser 0.42 adds saved flows: record a browser task once, then replay it - HTTP first, in-page second, recorded commands last
items.subheader: Experimental in the Vercel Labs CLI released on GitHub Monday; the update also trims MCP tool arguments and now requires Node 22.

items.title: Carb-loading, settled(ish): a 63-trial meta-analysis says eat 8+ grams per kilo for 36-48 hours before a marathon
items.subheader: Quantity beat duration - loading past 48 hours added nothing; a hard session plus high-GI carbs can compress it to 24-36 hours. Caveat: only 12% of the 641 participants were women.

items.title: Brian Chesky gives SF parks $100 million, the city's largest-ever single donation - pools open Sundays, stalled parks jump the queue
items.subheader: First $39M goes to five projects in SoMa, the Mission, Bayview, Potrero Hill and the Embarcadero; SoMa's Rachele Sullivan Park now opens in 2028 instead of 2031, and Garfield Pool adds 500 swim hours a year.

quotes.text: There is something truly special here in San Francisco. Much of my success, I attribute to the magic, and to the community, that is San Francisco.
quotes.by: Brian Chesky, Airbnb co-founder and CEO

items.title: Prop I social-housing measure loses 52-48 after $2.8M in real-estate opposition; Lurie-backed Prop C passed with 82%
items.subheader: Prop I would have earmarked half the $10M-plus property transfer tax for social housing; Prop C instead grows the affordable housing trust fund toward $125 million a year. Michael Moritz spent $200k on the fight.
items.image_alt: A MEDA affordable housing property in the Mission

items.title: California voters reject Prop 40's first-in-the-nation billionaire wealth tax after a tech-funded opposition campaign
items.subheader: The 5% net-worth tax failed after opponents, including Gov. Newsom, argued it would drive ultrawealthy taxpayers out of the state - a result with 2028 overtones.

items.title: Federal judge orders ICE to release UC Berkeley student detained at SFO, ruling her due-process rights were violated
items.subheader: Paula Albornoz Hernandez, 23, a Colombian asylum seeker with a valid work permit, was seized Oct. 30 boarding a flight; nearly 300 students rallied at Sproul Plaza, and 30 Bay Area officials wrote in support. Her asylum case continues.
items.image_alt: Paula Albornoz Hernandez (courtesy of her attorney)

quotes.text: This is a moment to remember what's possible when our community comes together to support one of our own.
